=== SEGMENT ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p350 | source ISLAHI-TADABBUR | verses 35:19-28 | Sūrah Sajdah ===
Sūrah Sajdah
Verses 23-26 are parenthetical in nature and address the Prophet Muh@ammad
(sws). Once they ended, the discourse switches to its original theme. It is stated
that do not people see that God sends down rain from the heavens and as a
result what is produced is not the same; things of different sorts and colour are
produced. Thus beautiful, colourful and tasty fruits are borne at some places,
while at some others defective and thorny bushes sprout. Same is the case with
this divine rain in the form of the Qur’ān. Through it the abilities and potentials
of the righteous develop while the evil found in others is exposed. This is
because Satan will not easily put up with the Qur’ān; he will in fact instigate
his followers to oppose it. The word ُانَوْلَأُ does not merely occur in Arabic to
mean “colour”; it also means “types” and “sorts”. In the next portion of this
verse also, the word is used in this very meaning.
In Sūrah A‘rāf, this aspect of the effects of rain is mentioned thus:
ُدَلَبْالَو ُبِّیَّالط ُجُرْخَی ُهُاتَبَن ِنْذِإِِب ِهِّبَر يِذَّالَو َثُبَخ َلَا ُجُرْخَی َّلَاِإِ اًدِكَن )7 :58(
And  the  land  which  is  fertile,  then  with  the  directive  of  its  Lord  its
vegetation looks good and the land which is defective bears vegetation
which is defective. (7:58)
Readers are advised to look up my explanation of the above verse.
Consider now, the last part of the verse: َنِمَو ِالَبِجْال ٌدَدُج ضٌ یِب رٌْمُحَو ٌفِلَت ْخُّم اَهُانَوْلَأُ
ُبیِابَرَغَو ودُسٌ The word  ٌدَدُج is the plural of  ٌةَّدُج and is used for the stripes of
various colours found on the backs of deer and mules; however, here it is used
for large rocks and stone tablets whose stripes or rows are found in mountains.
The word ُبیِابَرَغ is the plural of بْیِب ْرَغ.It means “jet black.” It is generally
used to emphasize the word  دَوْسأُ black). Thus if it is said that something is
بْیِب ْرَغ دَوْسأُ it would mean that it is jet black. The question then arises is that
why then does the word  ُبیِابَرَغ occur before  دْوُسThis is because placing a
word of emphasis before the noun it qualifies is against eloquence. Linguists
have given different  answers to this question. Some say that it is a  badal
(permutative) that occurs as an explication. If this interpretation is accepted,
then it is true that a badal that comes for explication in fact denotes emphasis.
In this case, it is as if the speaker repeats his statement in simple words so that
it can be etched in the minds. The reason why black rocks and stones are
referred to here with this emphasis is that just as there are black rocks in
mountains, similarly, there are people among human beings who have black
hearts; just as black rocks and white and red ones have separate uses, similarly,

In these verses, attention is foremost directed to the signs found in the earth.
Details can be seen in earlier sūrahs how various testimonies are drawn from
enlivening a dead piece of land on the Hereafter, monotheism and revelation of
divine guidance. Here, the aspect of providence is specially highlighted and
after that the right to show gratitude to God is asked for which is necessarily
imposed on people. The necessary consequence of this right is that people
worship God alone. This is because the favours they have been blessed with
are  neither  the  result  of  their  own  endeavours  nor  any  other  being  is
responsible to give them these favours.
The words ٌةَیآ in ٌةَیآَو ُمُهَّل ُض ْرَ ْلأَا ُةَتْیَمْال  is not defined to show its great

reflect, they will see that it is not merely grains which have been arranged for 
their livelihood, He has also caused date-palms and vine-trees and other fruit 
orchards to grow and has made springs to keep them green.
The words واُلُكْأََیِل نِم ِہِرَمَث اَمَو ُهْتَلِمَع ْمِهیِدْیَأُ َلَاَفَأُ َونُرُكْشَی  state the obligation

gave them these favours without even being entitled to them so that they show

The style of the discourse since the preceding verses is in the first person. 
Hence, giving due consideration to this fact, if God was to be the antecedent of
the pronoun then the words should have been نِم اَنِارَمْثأُِ  or words to similar

n, the antecedent of the pronoun is رضأُ earth) that is
already in mention since the preceding verses. However, [in spite of the fact 
that رضأُ is a feminine noun in Arabic] here a masculine pronoun is used to 
refer to it on the principle of dominant element (‘alā sabīl al-taghlīb). 
According to a principle of the Arabic language, at times a pronoun occurs not 
with relation to the word but to the meaning it conveys. Several examples of 
this can be seen in the previous sūrahs. By using the masculine pronoun for
رضأُ the purpose is to refer to ُدَلَبْال ُبِّیَّالط This is because though rain not only 
irrigates dry and barren areas and those which are lush and fertile, only the 
latter bear vegetation. This topic is discussed in Sūrah A‘rāf in the following 
words: ُدَلَبْالَو ُبِّیَّالط ُجُر ْخَی ُهُاتَبَن ِنْذِإِِب ِهِّبَر يِذَّالَو َثُبَخ َلَا ُجُر ْخَی َّلَاِإِ اًدِكَن )7 :58(  (And the 
land which is fertile its vegetation really blooms with the directive of its Lord; 
and that which is defective always produce defective things.(7:58)) 
The words اَمَو ُهْتَلِمَع ْمِهیِدْیَأُ  form a parenthetical sentence, and convey a very
important reminder. The implication is that they should consume the fruits but
always remember that they were not the ones who brought these fruits into
existence; it was God Who did so. It is a reminder of this reality that induces a
person to show gratitude to God and it is this gratitude which is the foundation
of all religion. Those who are unaware of this reality think that they are entitled
to God’s favours and that they are a result of their own abilities. The result is
that instead of thanking God they are afflicted with arrogance and arrogance by
its nature is a cause of polytheism and all forms of spreading anarchy and
disorder in the society.

َانَحْبُس يِذَّال َقَلَخ َاجَوْزَ ْلأَا اَهَّلُك اَّمِم ُتِنبُت ُضْرَ ْلأَا ْنِمَو ْمِهِسُنفَأُ اَّمِمَو َلَا َونُمَلْعَی )36( 232
The word اجَوْزَأُ means “types”, “kinds” and also means “pairs”. Here it 
encompasses both meanings. There is variety and diversity in whatever is 
created from the earth and everything that is created from it also occurs in 
pairs. Similarly, one can see a lot of difference in the appearances, colours, 
statures and languages of human beings; at the same time, human beings too 
occur in pairs. Same is the case with that part of the universe which is beyond 
the access of our knowledge. If one takes a step ahead and reflects, one will 
come to see that there is a harmony of objective in its variety and accord in its 
discord. This shows that only one God reigns over all the universe; no one else 
can interfere in it. Exalted is God from any trace of polytheism, and every 
object of this universe bears witness to this.
Moreover,  another  thing  that  becomes  evident  is  that  when  every  thing
occurs in pairs to achieve its purpose, it is necessary that this world should also
have its counterpart; otherwise, this world will be a purposeless place. And it is
not possible that a wise being do something purposeless and meaningless. Thus
to fill the vacuum created by this world, He has created the next world.
The purport of the verse is that this universe through its very existence bears 
witness to monotheism and the Hereafter and that exalted is the Creator of this 
universe from doing something purposeless. The word َانَحْبُس occurs to absolve 
someone of all negative attributes. Here its occasion and context are very 
evident. 
ٌةَیآَو ْمُهَّل ُلْیَّالل ُخَلْسَن ُهْنِم َارَهَّالن اَذِإَِف مُه َونُمِلْظُّم )37(  233

great sign of God’s power, mercy, providence and monotheism. He enwraps it
with a cloth of light and the dazzling day appears for them. They can now do
their daily chores in it. Then God pulls away this cloth of light and people are
left in darkness so that they can take rest in it. If God does not enwrap the night
with the cloth of light, they will always remain in darkness and if He does not
pull away this cloth of light, they will never be able to receive rest and comfort
at night. This coming and going of the day and night and their harmony for the
benefit of the creation is a clear testimony to the fact that this world is not a

the All-knowing). In other words, neither has this world come into existence 
accidentally nor is it being run of its own accord. It is, in fact, the product of 
the planning of a being who is all-powerful, all-dominant and all-

universe: the moon. It neither controls nor governs itself. God has ordained

bunches of dates. These branches after drying up assume the same shape as the
one a moon has in its initial and final phases. This comparison is pointing to
the fact that the state of the moon whom these foolish people worship is that it
has to pass through various phases each month in which it becomes like a dry
thorn and becomes like a crooked dry twig of a palm-tree.
